A provider being unreachable fails the **sync job** (alarmed), not a post

reasoning: Both regions state a rule for the same condition and the rules are incompatible. The F4 assumption row says that when the provider is unreachable at S1 the post blocks until a rate is available, except under an explicit tenant last-good policy. The rate-source algorithm says the opposite for that same condition: the posting path never calls a provider, so a provider being unreachable fails the background sync job and raises an alarm rather than affecting any post, and it redefines FX_RATE_UNAVAILABLE to mean no acceptable local rate for the pair rather than a provider timeout. Under F4 a provider outage blocks posting; under inst-rs-local the same outage is invisible to posting until the local store goes stale. Step 1 of the algorithm carries a revision marker, so the algorithm was rewritten to be post-path-local and the assumption row was left behind.
proposed_fix: design/06-fx-multicurrency.md must update the F4 assumption row to match inst-rs-local — provider unreachability fails the sync job, and only the absence of an acceptable local rate blocks a post — since the row is now contradicted by the algorithm in its own document.
